title: VirtIO descriptor (16 bytes)
summary: A VirtIO device's virtqueue is an array of 16-byte descriptors. Each descriptor: 8-byte guest-physical address of the buffer, 4-byte length, 2-byte flags (NEXT, WRITE, INDIRECT), 2-byte next descriptor index (if NEXT or INDIRECT).

ext.summary: A VirtIO device's virtqueue is an array of 16-byte descriptors. Each descriptor: 8-byte guest-physical address of the buffer, 4-byte length, 2-byte flags (NEXT, WRITE, INDIRECT), 2-byte next descriptor index (if NEXT or INDIRECT).

structure.meaning: Length of the buffer in bytes.
VRING_DESC_F_NEXT (1): next field is valid. VRING_DESC_F_WRITE (2): buffer is device-writable. VRING_DESC_F_INDIRECT (4): buffer contains a list of descriptors.
Index of the next descriptor (if NEXT) or number of descriptors (if INDIRECT).

notes: Virtqueues are split into descriptor table, available ring, and used ring.
Available ring: driver writes descriptor chain heads; device reads them.
Used ring: device writes completed descriptor heads + bytes written; driver reads them.
Indirect descriptors allow a single request to reference many buffers (up to 2^15).
VirtIO is the standard paravirtual I/O interface for KVM/QEMU, Firecracker, Cloud Hypervisor, crosvm, etc.
